day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter train) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, ~€5.50). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk — After settling in, explore the iconic Jordaan district on foot. Stop at local cheese shops for free tastings, grab a stroopwafel from a street stall, and stroll along the picturesque Prinsengracht and Brouwersgracht canals. Free to walk; budget ~€5–8 for snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Wander along the Herengracht 'Golden Bend' canal at dusk for stunning views. Grab a budget dinner at a nearby Indonesian 'warung' or a Dutch broodje (sandwich) shop.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick broodje (Dutch sandwich) or stroopwafel near Centraal Station or in the Jordaan (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Warung Spang Makandra or similar Indonesian/Surinamese budget spot in the Jordaan — hearty rice dishes for ~€8–12

day_by_day.notes: Buy an OV-chipkaart at Schiphol for easy public transport throughout the trip. The Jordaan is walkable from most canal-area hotels. Keep evenings light on Day 1 due to travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Open from 09:00. Arrive early to beat crowds. Explore masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch) and Vermeer. Book tickets online in advance to save time and potentially get a slight discount (~€22.50 adult). Spend 2–3 hours inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vondelpark Picnic & Museumplein — After the Rijksmuseum, relax in Vondelpark (free entry), Amsterdam's most beloved green space. Pick up picnic supplies from a nearby Albert Heijn supermarket (~€5–7). Stroll back through Museumplein and admire the 'I Amsterdam' letters area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Leidseplein square area for lively street performers and budget dining options. Enjoy a traditional Dutch 'dagschotel' (dish of the day) at a local brown café (bruine kroeg).

meals.breakfast: Supermarket breakfast from Albert Heijn (yogurt, bread, fruit) ~€3–5
meals.dinner: Bruine kroeg (brown café) near Leidseplein — stamppot or dagschotel ~€10–14

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Rijksmuseum tickets at rijksmuseum.nl to avoid long queues, especially on weekends. The museum is about a 15–20 min walk or short tram ride from the Canal House hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — Opens at 09:00; timed entry tickets MUST be booked online well in advance (~€16). This deeply moving experience takes about 1–1.5 hours. Walk through the secret annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Located on Prinsengracht, very close to most canal-area hotels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free Canal Walk & Westerkerk — After the Anne Frank House, walk along the Prinsengracht and Keizersgracht canals. Visit the Westerkerk church (free entry or small fee for tower climb ~€9). Browse the Noordermarkt area (Monday antique market if open) and explore the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) shopping district for window browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset canal cruise — book a budget group boat tour (~€12–18) departing from near Centraal Station or the Jordaan. A 1-hour cruise offers beautiful evening views of the illuminated canal houses.

meals.breakfast: Café Papeneiland or similar local bakery near the Anne Frank House — coffee and pastry ~€5–7
meals.lunch: Vleminckx or a local falafel shop on Spuistraat — fries with sauce or falafel wrap ~€4–7
meals.dinner: FEBO (Dutch fast food automat) for a fun, authentic cheap eat, or Soup en Zo for hearty soup and bread ~€7–10

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets sell out weeks in advance — book immediately after planning your trip. The entire morning area is very walkable along the canals. Wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Van Gogh Museum Experience — Opens at 09:00. Pre-book tickets online (~€22 adult). Spend 2 hours immersed in the world's largest Van Gogh collection, including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Located next to the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein.
day_by_day.afternoon: De Pijp Neighborhood & Albert Cuyp Market — Take a short tram ride to the vibrant De Pijp district. Browse the Albert Cuyp Market (open Mon–Sat, free entry), Amsterdam's largest outdoor market. Sample budget street food: herring (haring) for ~€3–4, fresh stroopwafels, and Dutch fries. Explore the colorful streets.
day_by_day.evening: Heineken Experience or budget alternative — If interested in brewing history, the Heineken Experience is nearby (~€23, includes 2 drinks). Budget alternative: grab a local craft beer at a bar in De Pijp (Brouwerij Troost ~€4–5/beer) and enjoy the neighborhood vibe.

meals.lunch: Albert Cuyp Market street food — haring, stroopwafel, fries ~€6–9
meals.dinner: Surinamese restaurant in De Pijp (e.g., Roopram Roti) — generous portions for ~€8–12

day_by_day.notes: The Van Gogh Museum and Albert Cuyp Market can be combined efficiently as De Pijp is a short tram ride from Museumplein. The market closes around 17:00, so plan the afternoon accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Free Museum Morning — Visit the Amsterdam Museum (city history, free with some discount cards) or explore the free permanent collection at the Stedelijk Museum courtyard. Alternatively, walk along the Eastern Docklands (Oostelijke Eilanden) for striking modern architecture — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Canal Stroll & Souvenirs — Walk the full length of the Herengracht or rent a pedal boat (~€10–15/hour) for a DIY canal experience. Browse budget souvenir shops near Damrak or pick up Dutch cheese and chocolates from an Albert Heijn as gifts. Visit Dam Square and the Royal Palace exterior (free).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Jordaan — treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget meal at a Dutch or international restaurant. Then pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Bakery or café near the hotel — fresh bread and coffee ~€5–7
meals.lunch: Pannenkoekenrestaurant (Dutch pancake house) — savory or sweet pancakes ~€8–11
meals.dinner: Jordaan restaurant — Dutch bitterballen appetizer and a main course, budget ~€14–18 with a local beer

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and store luggage if needed. Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol Airport takes ~17 min by train (runs every 10–15 min, ~€5.50). Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. OV-chipkaart can be returned at the airport for a deposit refund.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk
experiences.description: Wander through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood, stopping at local cheese shops, stroopwafel stalls, and traditional Dutch brown cafes (bruine kroegen). Enjoy canal-side snacks including raw herring, bitterballen, and freshly made poffertjes while soaking in the authentic local atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40), then taxi or tram to Canal House Amsterdam. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the hotel neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk: After settling in, head out for a leisurely stroll through the iconic Jordaan district — just steps from most canal house hotels. Browse local cheese shops, pick up a stroopwafel from a street stall, admire the narrow canal bridges, and soak in the quintessential Amsterdam atmosphere. This is a perfect low-key introduction to the city after a travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Canal-side dinner and evening walk: Enjoy dinner at a cozy restaurant along the Prinsengracht or Brouwersgracht. After dinner, take a gentle evening stroll along the illuminated canals — the city is especially magical at dusk with lights reflecting on the water.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at Schiphol Airport before landing, or a light snack at the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: De Luwte (Leliegracht) — a charming canal-side café perfect for a first Dutch lunch; try the Dutch kroket sandwich or a fresh tosti. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Café Restaurant Amsterdam (Watertorenplein) or Bistro Bij Ons (Prinsengracht) — classic Dutch brasserie fare like stamppot or fresh fish in a cozy setting. Budget ~€25–35 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-schedule Day 1 — travel fatigue is real. Pre-book the Anne Frank House tickets online as soon as possible if not already done, as they sell out weeks in advance. Pick up a multi-day GVB transit card (€9.50 for 3 days) at Centraal Station to save on tram fares.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: Start early with your pre-booked time slot (aim for 9:00–10:00 AM entry) at the Anne Frank House on Prinsengracht. This deeply moving and historically significant experience takes about 60–90 minutes. The museum is a short walk from most canal house hotels in the area. Arrive 10 minutes before your slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rijksmuseum Visit: After a light lunch, head to the Rijksmuseum in Museum Square (Museumplein). Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier collection, including Rembrandt's 'Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and stunning Dutch Golden Age artifacts. The museum's grand architecture and garden courtyard are themselves worth seeing. Book tickets online in advance (~€22.50 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Museumplein & Leidseplein area: Relax in Vondelpark (a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum) if weather permits, then head to the lively Leidseplein square for dinner and evening entertainment. The area has a great mix of mid-range restaurants and buzzing café terraces.

meals.breakfast: Buffet or continental breakfast at the hotel, or visit Winkel 43 on the Noordermarkt (famous for their apple pie) — a Sunday morning Amsterdam institution. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Café Papeneiland (Prinsengracht, near Anne Frank House) — a historic Dutch brown café serving sandwiches and soups since 1642. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Brasserie Keyzer (Van Baerlestraat, near Museumplein) — a classic Amsterdam brasserie with Dutch and European cuisine; great for a sit-down evening meal. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House MUST be pre-booked online — walk-in tickets are virtually impossible to get. Sunday mornings at the Noordermarkt (Jordaan) feature a wonderful organic farmers market if you pass through. Rijksmuseum is closed on select holidays — verify hours ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Van Gogh Museum Experience: Open at 9:00 AM — book the first entry slot to beat crowds. Spend 2–2.5 hours immersed in the world's largest Van Gogh collection, including 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and 'Almond Blossom.' The chronological layout tells the story of his life beautifully. Located right next to the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein. Tickets ~€22 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour: After lunch, embark on a private or small-group canal boat tour departing from the city center. Glide through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring, passing 17th-century merchant houses, hidden gardens, and iconic bridges. Tours typically last 60–90 minutes and offer a completely different perspective of the city. Many operators depart near Centraal Station or Leidseplein. Cost ~€20–35 per person for a group tour.
day_by_day.evening: De Pijp neighborhood exploration: Take tram to the vibrant De Pijp district — Amsterdam's bohemian quarter. Browse the Albert Cuyp Market stalls (closes around 5 PM on weekdays), then settle in for a relaxed dinner at one of the neighborhood's excellent mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Scandinavian Embassy (Sarphatipark, De Pijp) or hotel breakfast — excellent specialty coffee and open-faced sandwiches. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: Café Loetje (Johannes Vermeerstraat) — legendary for their Dutch steak sandwiches and casual atmosphere; a local favorite near Museumplein. Budget ~€12–18.
meals.dinner: Brouwerij Troost (Cornelis Troostplein, De Pijp) — a popular craft brewery and restaurant with hearty Dutch-inspired dishes; great atmosphere and locally brewed beers. Budget ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Van Gogh Museum tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially on Mondays when some other museums are closed. For the canal boat, compare operators like Those Dam Boat Guys, Lovers Canal Cruises, or Blue Boat Company for best value. May weather in Amsterdam can be changeable — bring a light jacket for the boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Canal Ring on Foot — Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes): Spend the morning wandering the charming 'Nine Streets' (Negen Straatjes) area — a grid of nine small streets connecting the main canals, lined with independent boutiques, vintage shops, antique dealers, and specialty cafés. This is the quintessential Amsterdam neighborhood experience, perfect for browsed shopping and canal photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Foam Photography Museum & Eastern Canal Ring: Visit Foam (Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam) on Keizersgracht — an intimate and world-class photography museum housed in a canal house (~€14 entry). Afterward, walk along the elegant Herengracht ('Gentleman's Canal') toward the Golden Bend, where Amsterdam's wealthiest 17th-century merchants built their grandest homes. End at the Amstel River for sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Rembrandtplein & Nightlife Area: Head to Rembrandtplein — Amsterdam's lively entertainment square — for dinner and evening drinks. The square is surrounded by a wide range of restaurants and café terraces. If interested, check listings for a live jazz performance at Bimhuis or a classical concert at the nearby Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at the hotel or Dignita Hoftuin (Nieuwe Spiegelstraat) — a social enterprise café with excellent eggs and coffee. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.lunch: Gartine (Taksteeg, near the Spui) — a hidden gem tearoom serving beautifully prepared sandwiches, soups, and salads using market-fresh ingredients. Tiny and beloved — arrive early. Budget ~€14–18.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Moeders ('Mothers') on Rozengracht — a beloved Amsterdam institution serving traditional Dutch home-cooking in a quirky, photo-lined interior. Iconic and affordable. Budget ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Gartine is very small and popular — either arrive right at opening (noon) or expect a short wait. The Nine Streets area is best explored on a weekday morning when it's less crowded. If you enjoy cycling, today is a great day to rent a bike (~€12–15/day from MacBike or Starbikes) to cover more ground along the canals.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Noord & NDSM Wharf (optional alternative: Begijnhof & Spui): Take the free ferry from behind Centraal Station to Amsterdam Noord for a taste of the city's creative, post-industrial side. Visit the NDSM Wharf (a converted shipyard with street art and studios) or the EYE Film Museum with its striking modern architecture and free panoramic views of the IJ waterway. Return by ferry in time for lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Canal Stroll & Souvenirs: Spend the afternoon at a relaxed pace — revisit a favorite canal street, pick up Dutch souvenirs (Delftware, stroopwafels, jenever gin) from the Jordaan or Nine Streets area. Visit the Westerkerk church tower (if open) for panoramic city views (~€9). Pack bags and check out if needed, storing luggage at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in the Jordaan: End your Amsterdam trip with a special dinner in the Jordaan — the city's most romantic and picturesque neighborhood. Choose a canal-view table if possible and toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Brasserie Blazer (Spui area) — a classic Amsterdam brown café with eggs, fresh bread, and strong coffee. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: IJ-Kantine (Amsterdam Noord, NDSM Wharf) — a large, lively canteen with great views of the IJ river and a rotating menu of fresh, affordable dishes. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Toscanini (Lindengracht, Jordaan) — a beloved upscale Italian restaurant in the Jordaan; book in advance as it's very popular. Alternatively, La Oliva (Egelantierstraat) for outstanding pintxos and Spanish wines in a cozy canal-house setting. Budget ~€30–45 per person for a special farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: The free GVB ferry to Noord runs 24/7 and is itself a lovely mini canal experience. If departing the next morning, confirm checkout time with Canal House Amsterdam and arrange airport transport — the train from Centraal to Schiphol is the most reliable option (~17 min, runs every 10–15 minutes). Toscanini requires reservations well in advance — book online before your trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight KL lands at 13:00, so the morning is reserved for travel. Take a private transfer from Amsterdam Schiphol Airport to Canal House Amsterdam. Enjoy a welcome drink and settle into your luxury canal-view suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour: After freshening up, embark on a private canal boat tour of Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, hidden gardens, and iconic bridges at a leisurely pace with a knowledgeable private guide and onboard refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Jordaan Neighborhood Stroll & Dinner: Take a gentle evening walk through the charming Jordaan neighborhood, soaking in the golden-hour light on the canals. Dine at Restaurant Breda (Reestraat), a refined Dutch-French bistro beloved for its seasonal tasting menus and intimate atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the flight or a light welcome spread at Canal House Amsterdam upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bites and drinks served aboard the private canal boat — charcuterie, local cheeses, and Dutch bitterballen.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Breda (Reestraat 26, Jordaan) — seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. The canal boat tour can typically be booked for a 2–3 hour afternoon slot departing near the hotel. Jet lag tip: stay active this afternoon to help adjust to local time.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Begin the day with a premium early-access visit to the Rijksmuseum, the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and Delftware collections. Opt for a private guided tour to gain deep insight into the Dutch Golden Age masterpieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience: A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, spend the afternoon immersed in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including 'Sunflowers' and 'The Bedroom.' Book a premium timed-entry ticket or private curator-led tour for an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ciel Bleu: Conclude the day with dinner at Ciel Bleu, the two-Michelin-starred restaurant on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura Amsterdam. Enjoy panoramic city views alongside exquisite French-Dutch haute cuisine and an award-winning wine list.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — enjoy a full Dutch breakfast spread in the elegant dining room overlooking the canal.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Rijksmuseum's Grand Café or the museum's premium restaurant, Rijks — known for its modern Dutch cuisine with local seasonal ingredients.
meals.dinner: Ciel Bleu at Hotel Okura (Ferdinand Bolstraat 333) — two-Michelin-star tasting menu. Reservations essential; book weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum tickets well in advance — both sell out quickly. Consider hiring a private art historian guide for the Rijksmuseum morning session for a truly premium experience. Both museums are within walking distance of each other in the Museumplein area.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: Start with a deeply moving visit to the Anne Frank House, walking through the historic hiding place of Anne Frank and her family during World War II. Book a premium time-slot ticket in advance. The experience is intimate, reflective, and historically profound.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk: After the emotional morning, decompress with a curated food and canal walk through the Jordaan. Visit artisan cheese shops, sample stroopwafels, explore local galleries, and browse the charming Noordermarkt area. Consider a private food guide for insider recommendations.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Canal Dinner Cruise: Board a private luxury dinner boat for a sunset cruise along the Prinsengracht and Herengracht canals. Enjoy a bespoke multi-course dinner prepared onboard with fine Dutch wines as the city's bridges and historic facades glow in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Winkel 43 (Noordermarkt) — famous for their Dutch apple pie; a beloved Jordaan institution perfect before the Anne Frank House visit nearby.
meals.lunch: During the Jordaan food walk — tastings of aged Gouda, herring, stroopwafels, and jenever (Dutch gin) at curated local stops.
meals.dinner: Private luxury canal dinner cruise — multi-course catered dinner aboard a private boat. Arrange through the hotel concierge or a specialist like 'Flagship Amsterdam.'

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets must be purchased online in advance — they release tickets exactly two months before the visit date and sell out within minutes. The Jordaan walk and Anne Frank House are both very close to Canal House Amsterdam, making this a highly walkable day.

day_by_day.morning: Stedelijk Museum & Vondelpark Morning: Visit the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam's world-class modern and contemporary art museum, featuring works by Mondrian, Kandinsky, and Warhol. Afterward, take a leisurely stroll through the adjacent Vondelpark — Amsterdam's most beloved green space.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Antiquarian & Canal House Tour: Arrange a private guided tour of one of Amsterdam's historic canal houses, such as the Museum Van Loon or the Willet-Holthuysen Museum, offering a rare glimpse into 17th-century patrician life along the Golden Bend of the Herengracht. Browse luxury antique dealers along Nieuwe Spiegelstraat afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails & Fine Dining in De Pijp: Head to the vibrant De Pijp neighborhood for pre-dinner cocktails at a craft cocktail bar, then dine at Ron Gastrobar, a relaxed yet refined one-Michelin-star restaurant by celebrated chef Ron Blaauw, known for accessible luxury dining.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — request a private breakfast service with fresh pastries, smoked salmon, and fresh-pressed juices delivered to your room.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Americain (Leidseplein) — a stunning Art Deco grand café with a sophisticated all-day menu; a true Amsterdam landmark.
meals.dinner: Ron Gastrobar (Sophialaan 55) — one-Michelin-star, relaxed fine dining with creative Dutch-French dishes. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Museum Van Loon and Willet-Holthuysen are both on the Keizersgracht/Herengracht canal belt — easily reachable by foot or canal bike from the hotel. Nieuwe Spiegelstraat is the city's premier antique and art gallery street, ideal for luxury souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Keukenhof Day Trip (Seasonal) or Hermitage/FOAM Photography Museum: If tulips are still in bloom in mid-May, take a private chauffeured day trip to Keukenhof Gardens (30 min from Amsterdam) — the world's most spectacular flower garden. Alternatively, visit FOAM Photography Museum on the Keizersgracht for a world-class photography exhibition in a beautifully converted canal house.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Shopping & Spa: Spend the afternoon exploring Amsterdam's luxury shopping streets — P.C. Hooftstraat for designer boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Chanel) and the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) for unique Dutch designers and concept stores. Finish with a treatment at the Canal House Amsterdam spa or a nearby luxury wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Bord'Eau: Celebrate your final evening in Amsterdam with a grand farewell dinner at Bord'Eau in Hotel de l'Europe, a two-Michelin-starred restaurant perched elegantly on the Amstel River. Indulge in a chef's tasting menu with sommelier-paired wines, with stunning views of the illuminated canal.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — linger over a full Dutch-European spread in the canal-side dining room.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café de Klepel (Nine Streets area) or a chic sandwich and wine at Broodje Bert — a local favorite for premium Dutch open-faced sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Bord'Eau at Hotel de l'Europe (Nieuwe Doelenstraat 2–14) — two-Michelin-star tasting menu on the Amstel River. The ultimate Amsterdam fine dining farewell. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Keukenhof is typically open late March to mid-May — confirm bloom status and opening dates closer to travel. If the gardens have closed, FOAM Museum is an excellent alternative. P.C. Hooftstraat is a 10-minute taxi ride from the hotel. Check out arrangements with the hotel concierge and arrange a private transfer to Schiphol if departing the following morning.

query: Amsterdam museums and canals, $2200 solo, 5 days, May 2027, from NYC
